title: Terri Roberts resigns from FFG and is walked out; alleged $59,000 ILO account transfer
who: Terri Roberts (former FFG support coordinator / Service Manager); Vida Reid; Leah Norman; Pieter Rossouw; DFG Legal
what: Roberts resigned on a Sunday in Oct 2021 citing participant risk, bullying, unethical practices and unpaid bonuses; next day Vida had packed her belongings and walked her out. Per Vida's improper-purpose submissions draft, Roberts left in disputed circumstances, handled through DFG Legal between Oct 2021 and Mar 2022; Roberts and partner Rossouw associated with Infinity Living Options; Roberts became 'Business Advisor' of Nurse Assist 24/7 (director Amanda Damon). Both Roberts and Norman gave statements to NDIS investigators on 11 Oct 2022, about twelve months later.

title: Tom & Co lodge joint 11-page submission for FFG and Vida against revocation and bans

Responses: Allegation 3 (unregistered SDA) - FFG only promoted SDA partners Yaran Property Group and Ability Housing (Facebook 18 Jul and 28 Sep 2022) and refers enquiries to Infinity Living Options Pty Ltd, in which 'our Clients have a shareholding'; Allegations 4-5 (30+ complaints, no complaints system) - no particulars, lists FFG policies, feedback@ffg.net.au; Allegation 6 - counsellor Sally See holds Masters in Sexology and Counselling Practice, no ACA/AHPRA registration but PCFA (claimed equivalent); Allegation 7 (threats/bullying) - Alexsis Bott 10 Jun 2022, Sarah-Jane Clulow 1 Jul 2022, Corina Abraham 15-19 Jun 2022 ($4,000 exit fee; 19 Jun email citing 'abusive manner of our staff'), Janeece Ferreira non-compete 16 Jun 2022, Hybrid Hive/The Hive said to be separate; Allegation 8 (false claims, Tiffany Rose, Andrew Hahn) - denied, criminal proceedings, with eviction timeline (10 Mar, 31 Mar DFG Legal letter, 12-13 Apr 2022) and assertions Hahn was violent and threatened Meghan Goodwin with a samurai sword; Allegation 9 (Goodwin third-party consent) - consent given long ago, Terri Roberts acting. title: Cassandra Burke statement taken by NDIA investigators (T62.1)
who: Cassandra Lee Burke, Support Coordinator at Access Disability Services (ex-FFG Jun/Jul-Oct 2022); statement taken by Bruce Graydon, NDIA Fraud Investigator, with NDIA investigator Narelle Richardson

Burke worked at FFG from Jun/Jul 2022 (receptionist, then support coordinator after 3 weeks, ~18 participants), joined Access in Oct 2022. Alleges: Vida's 30 Sep 2022 meeting announcing a work-from-home trial ('This is Simon's idea'); 4 Oct 2022 meeting on 'fraud claims' as defamation; on 15 Nov 2022 participant Jonathon Shapiera said Blake Sadler would be 'running a company for Vida and Simon called Dream Big'; Shapiera termination email 1 Dec 2022 4:53pm; Pamela Cricelli cancelled Giuseppe Cricelli's services (9/10 Dec 2022) as 'going back to Vida and Simon'; on 1 Dec 2022 outside the Jull St office, with Virginie Fanny-Dulloo present, Vida offered Burke a job at 'my new company'. title: Leathem internal review decision broadens Simon's banning order
who: Sian Leathem, Complaints Commissioner and delegate of the NDIS Commissioner (IR (7) 22/23, ICM23/100, D23 56430)
what: s 100 decision VARYING the 21 Dec 2022 order to 'no involvement with or in the NDIS sector, in any capacity', expressly prohibiting providing supports/services directly or indirectly to NDIS participants, providing labour hire workers to NDIS providers, and providing support, funding, guidance or assistance of any form to a provider. Findings: original decision correct/preferable but weighing disagreed; Simon associated with Hybrid Hive (ABN 96 651 140 108; banned permanently 21 Dec 2022) and FFG (revoked, 10-year ban 20 Dec 2022); co-director of Hybrid 17 Feb-21 Aug 2022 then sole director; co-director of FFG 28 Aug 2020-3 Jan 2021 and again from 1 Nov 2022; SoMF (19 Oct 2022) alleges Simon and Vida joint signatories on Hybrid's ANZ account; 20 Assist-submitted claims for Meghan Goodwin 25 Jan-10 May 2022 paid $78,491.06 to Assist then to Hybrid's ANZ account; Assist filed 11 suspicious-invoice reports 26 Aug-21 Sep 2022. Excluded: Clulow claims (Simon not FFG director then), the $1,485,527 expired-plan figure (minimal weight), Vida's bail conditions, duplicated allegations, FFG conduct generally. Rejects procedural-fairness complaint (opportunities on 2 Dec 2022, 6 Feb and 22 Mar 2023 unused); directors answer for the entity; no weight to unproduced exculpatory evidence, minimal weight to Simon's 'wholesale denial'. Treats as new evidence the 29 Oct 2022 ASIC Form 201 for Dream Big, the 9 Feb 2023 Vitality WA recruitment email and Burke's statement; para 46 finds Simon 'not suitable at this time to be an NDIS provider' given the ongoing NDIA and law-enforcement investigation, with five years said to match the time expected for those processes to conclude. Reviewer admissions at [32]-[33]: the original decision-maker at times attributed liability for conduct during a period Simon was not director of Hybrid or FFG and considered the same facts twice, and the reviewer states "I have not considered or given weight to such material"; para 29(i) Clulow-related FFG claims (24 Nov 2021-22 Jun 2022) cannot be attributed to Simon; para 29(j) $1,485,527 expired-plan figure given minimal weight because the NDIA Tactical Intelligence Report of 18 Aug 2022 acknowledges the proportion for services actually provided is unknown. Decision under review in ART 2023/3363.

title: Leathem internal review decision reduces FFG ban from 10 to 3 years
who: Sian Leathem, Complaints Commissioner and delegate of the NDIS Commissioner under s 100 (IR (10) 22/23, ICM23/198)
what: Internal review decision VARYING the 20 Dec 2022 s 73ZN(1)(a) banning order against FFG from 10 years to 3 years (5:30pm 20 Dec 2022 to 12:00am 21 Dec 2025 AWST), 3 years approximating the time expected for FFG-related criminal proceedings, after which it can be revisited (s 73ZO). Decision letter to Tom Monks; Attachment A varied order; Attachment B statement of reasons (76 paras). Review request received 21 Feb 2023; Monks' submission 20 Mar 2023; decision due 22 May 2023 so made outside s 100(6A) (acknowledged). Penalty for breach s 73ZN(10) up to 1,000 penalty units x5 for a corporation = $1,375,000; AAT review within 28 days (AAT Act s 29(3)(b)(i)); contact Pascal Moussa. Leathem finds the original decision correct and preferable but disagrees with its reasoning: original reused revocation reasons rather than giving independent ban reasons and relied on a broader range of material than needed; she decides on a narrower basis (fraud only; other allegations 'fallen away'). She concedes 'deficiencies and failings' of the original decision-maker (Philip Halton, not named): not sufficiently informing FFG of some allegations (though 'on balance adequately informed') and not clearly articulating his analysis or the reason for minimal weight to FFG's submissions (internal working documents show he did consider them); the 30 Nov 2022 submission wrongly alleged no response to the extension request (Commission email 15 Nov 2022 6:04pm from WACompliance to info@tomandcolegal.com.au attached the extension letter). Evidence recited: complaints 4-37380907579 (10 May 2022, Goodwin), 4-38279458621 (PCI/NDIA referral 10 Aug 2022, Elanor Smith), 4-37833786005 (20 May 2022, Clulow $7,500); sworn statements of Clulow (11 Oct 2022 paras 13-18) and Goodwin (12 Oct 2022 paras 25-26; minimal weight); Prosecution Notice 18 Oct 2022 and NDIA SoMF 19 Oct 2022 charging Vida under Criminal Code (Cth) ss 400.9(1) (two counts) and 135.1(3) (two counts); ASIC extract; briefing notes EC22-002000 and EC22-002581; Leah Norman's allegations of inflating coordination time and 'invoice bombing'. SoMF allegations summarised: Vida and Simon joint signatories on FFG ANZ and Westpac accounts; 81 false payment requests against Goodwin/Clulow plans 26 Nov 2021-22 Jun 2022 (reasons typo '2020'); NDIA investigation began 1 Sep 2022; 30 Nov 2021 new Goodwin plan then three FFG claims within an hour (incl. 398 hours house cleaning 15 Oct-30 Nov 2021) paid $43,004.60 on 1 Dec 2021; Assist Plan Managers 14 claims ($5,979.64); forensic accountant $127,475.30 of Goodwin claims for no service, of which $78,491.06 went to Hybrid Hive (disregarded); Clulow claims $86,192.60 and $33,816.88, forensic $120,009.48 no service. Finds on the balance of probabilities FFG was 'used as a vehicle' for fraud by key personnel and that FFG provided no evidence to negate it. Background findings: FFG registered NDIS provider 19 Nov 2020-20 Dec 2022; Vida co-director 28 Aug 2020-3 Jan 2021, sole director 4 Jan 2021-20 Oct 2022, co-director 21 Oct-1 Nov 2022; Simon co-director 28 Aug 2020-3 Jan 2021 and again from 1 Nov 2022 to present.
to_whom: Tom Monks, Tom & Co Legal Pty Ltd, for FFG
how: s 100 internal review decision; varied banning order (Att A); statement of reasons (Att B); reviewable decision in ART 2023/4494
why: Per SoR: FFG used as vehicle for fraud on the balance of probabilities; 3 years = time expected for criminal proceedings; revocation alone does not safeguard (unregistered supports); proportionate per s 181D(4)(b).
quote: I am of the view that the original decision was the correct and preferable decision to be made, however, I disagree with the reasoning for the original decision.
people: Sian Leathem; Tom Monks; Pascal Moussa; Philip Halton; Sarah-Jane Clulow; Meghan Goodwin; Elanor Smith; Leah Norman; Vida Reid; Simon Reid

title: Commission (AGS) applies to stay all three AAT proceedings

why: Per letter: interests of justice where concurrent criminal proceedings exist.
